plan: Given my value of $39, I should bid slightly below it to maximize profit while considering rational behavior. Other bidders will likely bid near their values. To win, my bid should be higher than the expected third-highest bid. A bid of $38.9 balances winning probability and profit, assuming others bid close to their values.

Given my value of $27, I aim to bid just above the expected third-highest bid to maximize profit. Assuming rational behavior, bidders will bid slightly below their values. To win, I should bid slightly above $18, the expected value of the third-highest bid when values are uniformly distributed. This balances winning probability and profit margin.

Given my value of $13, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit while minimizing risk. Since the prize value is independently drawn, other bidders are likely to have different values. A rational bid slightly below $13, say $12.9, increases my chance of winning if others bid low, while not exceeding my value. This ensures I pay less than my value if I win, maximizing profit.
